topStories.headline: Fleet Week Descends on the Presidio: Road Closures, Packed Shuttles, and Three Days of Blue Angels
topStories.dek: The Navy's Blue Angels return to San Francisco Bay this weekend after a 2025 shutdown grounded them, with the Presidio bracing for its heaviest crowds of the fall.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Fleet Week runs October 4–12, and the marquee event — the Blue Angels air show — fills the sky directly over the Presidio and Marina waterfront on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, October 9 through 11, from noon to 4 p.m. each day. <cite index="49-4,49-5">The U.S. Navy's famed F/A-18 E/F Super Hornet squadron headlines the show, returning after a federal government shutdown grounded the team and halted all U.S. military participation during last year's event.</cite> <cite index="49-6">Also on the 2026 air show bill: the U.S. Marine Corps F-35B demo team and the U.S. Air Force F-22 Raptor demo team.</cite>

Residents and visitors heading to or through the Presidio this weekend should plan around significant disruptions. <cite index="2-10">Montgomery Street, Anza Street (from Lincoln to Graham), Mason Street (from Marina Boulevard), and Halleck Street close at noon on Saturday, October 10, and Sunday, October 11.</cite> <cite index="2-13">The Arguello Boulevard, Presidio Boulevard, Lombard Street, and Mason Street entrances will also close to cars at noon on Saturday and Sunday.</cite> <cite index="2-7,2-8">Parking will be extremely limited, especially near the waterfront, and paid parking with special event fees of $9 per hour and $45 per day will be in effect and enforced on Saturday and Sunday.</cite>

<cite index="2-1,2-2">The Presidio is adding service on the Downtown Route and the Presidio GO South Hills route on Saturday and Sunday, with the Downtown Route running every 15 minutes between 10 a.m. and 7:30 p.m.</cite> The Presidio and Fleet Week organizers strongly encourage visitors to use public transit or the shuttle rather than driving. <cite index="54-2">The Parade of Ships — billed as the largest on the West Coast — runs Friday, October 9, from 11 a.m. to noon along the San Francisco waterfront,</cite> viewable from the Presidio shoreline all the way to the Bay Bridge.

topStories.headline: Is the Richmond Becoming Too Hot to Handle? Residents and Businesses Weigh Rising Rents and New Arrivals
topStories.dek: A new analysis finds the once-overlooked Richmond District drawing upscale retailers and outside attention — while long-term tenants face rent hikes that can double their monthly costs overnight.
topStories.body:
<cite index="58-5">What's happening in the Richmond isn't staying in the Richmond.</cite> A piece published October 6 by Gazetteer SF examines the forces reshaping the neighborhood, from upscale grocery chains eyeing new outposts to a viral story earlier this year about an Outer Richmond family facing a 90-percent rent increase after their building changed hands. <cite index="58-6">Soon enough, Bi-Rite will be moving into a long-defunct space at 6001 California St. for its fourth location, a sign of gentrification to some and an answer to others' prayers.</cite>

<cite index="58-8,58-9,58-10">In a San Francisco Standard article that went viral in June, a couple in the Outer Richmond learned their landlord was increasing their rent by 90 percent. Ashley and Zachary Waldman's two-bedroom condo listed for $3,500 a month in 2021 — whoever moves in after them will rent the same place for $7,000 a month.</cite> The jump was enabled, reporting found, by the building's sale and a legal gray area around rent-control protections for units in buildings that changed ownership.

Rental data confirms the pressure is not isolated. <cite index="41-5">One-bedroom rents in the Richmond District rose roughly 61 percent year-over-year through September 2026.</cite> On the restaurant front, <cite index="29-1">the Berkeley original Rose Pizzeria, which the New York Times named one of America's best pizzerias, has opened its first San Francisco outpost at 1 Clement Street.</cite> And <cite index="15-8,15-9">a Chronicle reader poll published in August found the Richmond received the most votes among all neighborhoods Chronicle readers would most want to move to.</cite> Whether these arrivals signal a neighborhood thriving or one at a tipping point is a question residents, housing advocates, and the Rent Board will be watching closely in the months ahead.

topStories.headline: Richmond Station Gets Smaller: SFPD Redraws District Boundaries for First Time in a Decade
topStories.dek: New patrol boundaries took effect October 1 at six SFPD stations, with Richmond Station losing a stretch of Panhandle-adjacent territory to an expanded Park Station.
topStories.body:
<cite index="34-1">Effective 6 a.m. on October 1, 2026, the San Francisco Police Department implemented revised district station and patrol sector boundaries</cite> — the first such change in a decade, required under the city charter. <cite index="33-4,33-5">The changes affect the Central, Tenderloin, Northern, Southern, Richmond, and Park districts, and are part of the SFPD's mandatory 10-year review of district boundaries to help optimize police operations and efficiency.</cite>

For Richmond Station, the change means a smaller footprint. <cite index="38-8">Richmond Station decreases its coverage by removing the area between Stanyan Street on the west — along Geary Street and Fulton Street — to Divisadero Street on the east, which now falls under the expanded Park Station.</cite> Park Station, in turn, gains the Duboce Triangle and the North of Panhandle area. Elsewhere in the city, <cite index="34-5,34-6">Southern Station will assume responsibility for both sides of Market Street, and Central Station will assume responsibility for additional area westward to Van Ness Avenue.</cite>

<cite index="33-6">District station captains, command staff, city legislators, and community stakeholders worked with the police department to develop the new boundaries.</cite> <cite index="33-7">SFPD says the changes will not cause any disruption to service,</cite> though the department acknowledged that during the transition, officers responding to calls in newly reassigned areas may occasionally come from the prior district. Residents uncertain which station now covers their address can consult the updated boundary maps at sanfranciscopolice.org.

events.title: Clement Street Happy Hour Cleanup
events.location: Richmond Republic Draught House, 642 Clement St, Inner Richmond
events.description: <cite index="98-1,98-2,98-4,98-5">Join the Civic Joy Fund, Refuse Refuse, SF Public Works, and the community for a friendly neighborhood cleanup. Volunteers meet at Richmond Republic Draught House (642 Clement St) to grab supplies, clean from 4–5 p.m., then stay for free food and drinks.</cite> Sign up free at the Civic Joy Fund Mobilize page.

events.title: Fleet Week Air Show — Blue Angels over San Francisco Bay
events.location: San Francisco Bay / Marina Green (viewable from Presidio shoreline)
events.description: <cite index="53-2">The centerpiece of Fleet Week is the air show, October 9–11, with the U.S. Navy Blue Angels headlining between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz.</cite> Free from public areas; premium seats ticketed. See the Presidio's Fleet Week advisory for road closure and shuttle details before you go.

events.title: NPS Guided Walk: 250 Years on the Presidio
events.location: Presidio Visitor Center, 210 Lincoln Blvd, Presidio
events.description: <cite index="125-6,125-7,125-8">National Park Service rangers lead a free guided walk through Presidio Tunnel Tops and the historic Main Post, exploring the layered history of the park from the time of the Ohlone people through Spanish and U.S. Army occupation to its present role as a national park site.</cite> Flat route; all ages welcome.

events.title: Bea Arthur: The Documentary — Bay Area Premiere at the Balboa
events.location: Balboa Theater, 3630 Balboa St, Outer Richmond
events.description: <cite index="70-4,70-5">The Bay Area premiere of a new documentary offering an intimate look at the life and career of Emmy and Tony Award–winning performer Bea Arthur, built around a never-before-seen interview paired with new conversations from colleagues and friends.</cite> <cite index="70-9">A post-screening conversation with filmmaker and producer Dan Watt follows.</cite> Tickets $12.50–$15.

events.title: District 1 Richmond Family Summit
events.location: Richmond Recreation Center, 251 18th Ave, Inner Richmond
events.description: <cite index="107-7,107-8">Join the District 1 Family Summit at the Richmond Recreation Center — part of the This Is Your City: Family Summit Series, which invites families, caregivers, young people, and community members to help shape the future of San Francisco.</cite> <cite index="106-5">Free food, childcare, and interpretation are provided.</cite> Event runs 5:30–8 p.m.
events.sourceName: SF.gov / Our Children Our Families Initiative

moreNews.headline: Arguello Corridor Fatality Investigation Still Open — No Arrests
moreNews.body: As of this week, no arrests have been made in the September 28 death of an 80-year-old man struck by a tow truck at Anza Street and Arguello Boulevard — the collision that led last week's issue. <cite index="116-1">The crash marked the city's 13th pedestrian fatality of 2026, according to KRON.</cite> <cite index="115-7,115-8,115-9">SFPD's Traffic Collision Investigations Unit is leading the investigation; no arrests have been made, and the case remains open and active</cite> (Case #260-569-018). <cite index="117-9">The stretch of Arguello Boulevard north of Geary Boulevard remained on San Francisco's High Injury Network even after earlier safety treatments removed other portions of the road from that list.</cite> A funded safety improvement project for the corridor has not yet been completed.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: The original 1992 Inner Richmond location that popularized Burmese cuisine in San Francisco, famous for its tea leaf salad and perpetual lines.

restaurants.name: Mandalay Restaurant
restaurants.description: San Francisco's oldest running Burmese restaurant, open since 1984 and named a James Beard America's Classic in 2024.

restaurants.name: Dalida
restaurants.description: Upscale Eastern Mediterranean dining in the Presidio's Main Post, with a porch overlooking the parade lawn stretching toward Alcatraz.

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: A beloved Inner Richmond Turkish restaurant celebrated by sommeliers for its impeccable natural wine list and Eastern Mediterranean cooking.

restaurants.name: Lokma
restaurants.description: Cozy Outer Richmond spot serving a modern California-Turkish menu of shared plates in a brick-walled dining room with excellent brunch on weekends.

restaurants.name: Aziza
restaurants.description: Acclaimed Moroccan restaurant on Geary Boulevard serving inventive contemporary Moroccan cuisine in an elegant, warmly lit setting.

restaurants.name: Bella Trattoria
restaurants.description: Long-running Inner Richmond Italian restaurant specializing in cucina napolitana, with housemade pastas and a loyal neighborhood following since 1996.

restaurants.name: Fiorella
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Italian wine bar and pizzeria known for blistered wood-fired pies and a lively Outer Richmond dining room.

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Berkeley's nationally acclaimed pizzeria opened its first San Francisco outpost at the east end of Clement Street in April 2026, serving Neapolitan and Roman-style pies daily.

restaurants.name: Pizzetta 211
restaurants.description: Small, much-loved Outer Richmond pizzeria serving a short rotating menu of thin-crust seasonal pies in an intimate space with outdoor parklet seating.

restaurants.name: B Star
restaurants.description: Burma Superstar's sister restaurant offering a more eclectic, fusion-forward Burmese menu in a slightly more relaxed setting on Clement Street.

restaurants.name: Mamahuhu
restaurants.description: Bright and popular Clement Street spot serving approachable, flavor-forward Chinese-American dishes including mapo tofu and mala cucumbers.

restaurants.name: Hokkaido Sashimi Marketplace
restaurants.description: Inner Richmond counter serving fresh sashimi and to-go sushi rolls, a popular stop before a picnic in Golden Gate Park.

restaurants.name: Hard Knox Cafe
restaurants.description: Casual Outer Richmond diner serving Southern staples—fried chicken, cornbread muffins, and daily brunch until 3 p.m.—at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Kissaten Hi-Fi
restaurants.description: New Inner Richmond café rooted in the Japanese kissaten tradition, serving single-cultivar matcha and Filipino-inspired coffee in a slow, intentional setting.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: The first hotel to open inside the Presidio national park site, housed in a beautifully restored 1903 Georgian Revival building with bay-view suites, complimentary breakfast, and evening wine receptions.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Historic barracks building converted into a contemporary 42-room hotel on the Presidio's Main Post, offering free breakfast, forest and bay views, and a shuttle downtown.

hotels.name: Geary Parkway Motel
hotels.description: Renovated 20-room motel on Geary Boulevard offering free to-go breakfast and on-site parking within walking distance of Golden Gate Park.

shops.name: Green Apple Books
shops.description: Iconic Richmond District bookstore founded in 1967, stocking new and used titles across 8,000 square feet at the corner of Clement and Sixth Avenue.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.description: Inner Richmond design store and rotating gallery selling art books, locally made goods, prints, apparel, and limited-edition artist collaborations.

shops.name: Foggy Notion
shops.description: Inviting Clement Street boutique selling handcrafted ceramics, stationery, and locally made gifts with a warm, artisan-focused curation.

shops.name: Gaslight & Shadows Antiques
shops.description: Outer Richmond antique shop on Clement Street with a passionately curated selection of vintage objects and collectibles.

shops.name: Nijiya Market
shops.description: Well-stocked Japanese supermarket carrying fresh sushi-grade fish, Japanese pantry staples, and prepared foods popular with the neighborhood's Japanese community.

shops.name: New May Wah Supermarket
shops.description: Large Asian grocery destination on Clement Street with an extensive range of Chinese, Southeast Asian, and other imported pantry items.

shops.name: Jane Consignment
shops.description: Outer Richmond consignment shop on Clement Street carrying quality pre-owned women's clothing and accessories.

shops.name: Love Street Vintage
shops.description: Curated vintage clothing boutique on Clement Street carrying a wide selection of women's vintage apparel and accessories.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: Forty-thousand-square-foot museum in the Presidio dedicated to the life and legacy of Walt Disney, with ten interactive galleries, Disney film screenings, and a new exhibition opening October 23 tracing artist Eyvind Earle's career.

artEntertainment.name: Legion of Honor
artEntertainment.description: Beaux-Arts museum in Lincoln Park founded in 1924, housing 6,000 years of European art, over 70 Rodin sculptures, and one of the largest prints-and-drawings collections in the country.

artEntertainment.name: Park Life Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Contemporary art gallery and design store
artEntertainment.description: Inner Richmond gallery space behind the Park Life store mounting rotating exhibitions of local and national artists, with about ten shows per year.

artEntertainment.name: Avenue 12 Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Small Inner Richmond gallery active in the Bay Area arts community, exhibiting local artists and Bay Area subject matter.

artEntertainment.name: Andy Goldsworthy Sculpture Trail
artEntertainment.description: Four permanent works by British sculptor Andy Goldsworthy installed across the Presidio—Wood Line, Spire, Earth Wall, and Tree Fall—all freely accessible on foot.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: One of the oldest buildings in San Francisco, the adobe-walled Officers' Club on the Presidio's Main Post houses free museum galleries exploring the site's 250-year history.

gymsRecreation.name: Richmond District YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service YMCA branch in the Inner Richmond offering cardio equipment, weight rooms, yoga classes, and youth programs for the neighborhood.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Community YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: YMCA branch inside the Presidio offering fitness classes, youth programs, and access to the Letterman Aquatics Center pool.

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Intimate yoga studio at 182 Sixth Avenue offering vinyasa flow, power flow, prenatal yoga, and $15 community classes as part of San Francisco's largest locally owned yoga network.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot Yoga Plus
gymsRecreation.description: Outer Richmond studio on Geary Boulevard specializing in Bikram 26&2 yoga and Inferno Hot Pilates in a heated environment.

gymsRecreation.name: The Yoga Shala SF – Balboa Street
gymsRecreation.description: Richmond-area heated vinyasa yoga studio on Balboa Street, created for practitioners to thrive through consistent, community-oriented practice.

gymsRecreation.name: F45 Training
gymsRecreation.description: Franchise functional fitness studio on Geary Boulevard offering fast-paced group circuit workouts with attentive form coaching.

gymsRecreation.name: Live Fit Gym – Inner Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Community gym at Arguello Boulevard offering strength training, power flow yoga, and fitness classes led by instructors including a licensed doctor of physical therapy.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: Consistently ranked among the nation's top public courses, this 18-hole championship layout winds through eucalyptus and Monterey pine in the Presidio national park.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park
gymsRecreation.description: More than 1,000 acres of meadows, trails, sports courts, and cultural institutions bordering the Richmond neighborhoods, used daily for running, cycling, tennis, and lawn sports.
